item.title: When Observation Changes Reality: The Quantum Enigma of the Double-Slit Experiment
item.description: In the early 1800s, Thomas Young conducted a simple experiment with light that changed physics forever. item.title: Brain-Machine Interfaces: Connecting Minds to Machines
item.description: Imagine controlling a computer, a robotic arm, or even typing text—using only your thoughts. This is the promise of Brain-Machine Interfaces (BMIs), also known as Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCIs). A BMI is a direct communication pathway between the human brain and an external device. It works by detecting brain signals, interpreting them, and translating them into commands that machines can understand. item.title: The Multiverse: Are We Living in Just One of Many Universes?
item.description: When we look up at the night sky, we see billions of stars, galaxies, and clusters stretching across unimaginable distances. It feels endless. But what if our entire universe —with all its galaxies, black holes, and cosmic wonders—is just one among countless others? This is the mind-bending idea of the multiverse. What Is the Multiverse? The multiverse is the hypothesis that reality is much larger than what we can observe, and that our universe is just one “bubble” in a far greater cosmic foam.
